preamble: Glottalization of the voiceless lateral fricative [ɬ] by fusion with a following uvular stop. Beck (2000) shows that in Upper Necaxa Totonac Proto-Northern Totonac *q became a glottal stop and the resulting fricative + glottal stop sequences collapsed into ejective fricatives: *ɬq > *ɬʔ > ɬʼ. Upper Necaxa ɬʼ corresponds to ɬq in Apapantilla, Papantla and Zapotitlan Totonac. The same change produced sʼ from *sq and šʼ [ʃʼ] from *šq. Beck also notes that the Upper Necaxa ejective fricatives lower neighbouring vowels just as q does in the other languages, and that fricative + ʔ sequences formed later across a morpheme boundary stay as two consonants. He describes the result, ejective fricatives with no ejective stops, as to his knowledge unique among the world's languages; Wikipedia, citing Beck (2006), confirms that *q became a glottal stop and that *sq, *ʃq and *ɬq collapsed into ejective fricatives. The evidence comes from one language.
